name: Tajikistan
summary_text: Tajikistan is dangerous for trans visitors. Same-sex conduct is legal, but police conducted a series of raids against LGBTIQ people in several cities in 2022-2023, and documentation (IPHR 2024) shows systematic patterns: discrimination in all spheres, police abuse, arbitrary detention, and forced disclosure. There is no transparent legal gender recognition (a medicalised registration route exists on paper under the Civil Status Acts law), no anti-discrimination protection, and authorities have previously maintained informal registries of LGBT citizens. For a visitor: no expression statute, but police raids + registry practices + zero recourse make discovery dangerous.

sources.claim_summary: IPHR report 'Rights for All? LGBTIQ Persons in Tajikistan Systematically Denied Human Rights' (Feb 2024): documents widespread homophobia/transphobia, human-rights violations, the 2016 police register of LGBTIQ people, 2022/2023 police raids with forced HIV-testing and arbitrary criminal charges, ill-treatment, sexual abuse and extortion by police, privacy violations followed by 'pornography' prosecutions, and additional problems facing trans people.

sources.title: Tajikistan | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex acts not criminalised since independence; no SOGISC non-discrimination protections; no transparent legal gender recognition procedure, though at least two trans men and one trans woman changed markers via court in 2023; nonconsensual intersex interventions legal; in 2024 ECOM recorded 27 cases of human-rights violations against LGBT people, with police arbitrary arrests, blackmail and extortion.

ECOM study (2024) on trans people's access to medical services including HIV prevention/treatment and HRT across the EECA region (with country coordinators including Tajikistan), including information for trans migrants.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2025, Tajikistan chapter (covering 2024): Russia's anti-LGBTI laws have influenced Tajikistan; coming out risks family shame leading to sham marriages - one person was beaten, tied up without food and forcibly married, with police taking no action; in Sughd, 10+ cases of police luring LGBT people into fake meetings to register them in a database and extort money; the 2022 anti-discrimination law dropped SOGI, leaving only 'sex'.

ECOM legislative analysis (2020): 'Legislative analysis related to SOGI and HIV in Tajikistan' - identifies legal barriers for gay men, other MSM and trans people, analysing legislation and law-enforcement practice against international standards, with local partners.

sources.title: World Report 2017: Tajikistan | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW World Report 2017, Tajikistan chapter: the human-rights situation deteriorated sharply in 2016 - opposition leaders sentenced, lawyers imprisoned, a predetermined referendum allowing President Rahmon to rule for life - the repressive context for LGBT life.

sources.title: Tajikistan Remains ‘Hell for Gays’ · Global Voices
sources.claim_summary: Global Voices (Jan 2013) by Alexander Sodiqov: 'Tajikistan Remains Hell for Gays' - despite decriminalisation 15 years earlier, there is very little tolerance; those who come out become targets of physical and psychological abuse including from police; the LGBT community remains 'one of the most closed and secretive parts of Tajik society'; sparked by a violent university incident.
